review: 1:2 חַיִּל — 'soldier'; the Arabic الْجُنْدِيّ is singular, and חַיִל is the biblical collective that can stand for one warrior in poetic address (cf. גִּבּוֹר חַיִל).
2:2 עִם־הֶאִיר הָאוֹר — 'when the light dawned', for عِنْدَ شُرُوقِ النُّور; the infinitive construct with עִם marks time, as in Gen 19:15.
2:4 בְּטַח בַּצּוּר אֲדֹנֵינוּ — the Arabic is 'trust our Lord, the Rock of ages'; Hebrew reverses the apposition because בְּטַח takes its object first, and צוּר carries 'Rock'.
3:1 עַד־שׁוּב אֲדֹנֶיךָ — the infinitive construct after עַד ('until your Lord returns') avoids a finite verb that would add a syllable.
3:2 וְיִמְצָאֲךָ גּוֹבֵר — 'and may He find you conquering'; the Arabic يَجِدْكَ is jussive after the imperative, and Hebrew keeps the same sequence.
